findings.summary: scripts/gates/m-1-complete.sh's own design explicitly leaves 'does an open backlog row bear on a non-negotiable' as a judgement call for whoever reads its output next to the backlog -- made now: M-1.38 (and its sibling M-1.39) are exactly such rows, since both are live, confirmed-present defects in scripts/check-reviewed.sh and lib.sh's known_task_ids(), the literal enforcement mechanism non-negotiable 4 names, so m-1-complete.sh reporting green (which it will, the moment this checkpoint's review artifact is staged) should not be read as license to mark M-1 'done' in roadmap.md while M-1.38 stands open.

findings.evidence: .pre-commit-config.yaml's hook entries read e.g. "non-negotiable 4: every commit is reviewed...", "non-negotiable 2: no threshold is read from an environment variable" as literal, hand-written text. scripts/gates/m-1-complete.sh's header: 'A hard-coded rule 1 -> check-commit-msg.sh table here would be a second place non-negotiable 1's own script name lives, and the two would drift the first time either changed without the other.' Nothing checks .pre-commit-config.yaml's labels against AGENTS.md's actual numbering; a future renumbering of the seven rules would leave these labels silently wrong, though the entry: scripts themselves (the actual enforcement) would be unaffected -- cosmetic only, hence minor.
findings.summary: .pre-commit-config.yaml (M-1.14) hand-lists which AGENTS.md non-negotiable number each hook enforces in its 'name:' field, the exact hand-maintained rule-to-script mapping m-1-complete.sh (M-1.16, written afterward) explicitly avoids by parsing AGENTS.md's Non-negotiables section instead -- citing that precise hazard in its own header.
